context: Options, cheapest first: (a) add a .gitattributes merge driver for the generated block so git resolves it by rerunning the generator instead of raising a textual conflict; (b) move the generated table into its own included file so conflicts are confined to a file nobody hand-edits; (c) drop the committed numbers and have CI compute them on demand, keeping only the prose. Do NOT resolve occurrences by hand-picking a side -- that is how wrong numbers land.
description: _project/specs/uat-framework.md carries a generated per-module Actual column and a UAT-LOC-SUMMARY block produced by _project/scripts/uat_loc_table.py and CI-checked with --check. Any PR that changes a UAT module's line count must regenerate that block, so two concurrent UAT PRs always collide there even when their code changes are disjoint. Observed 2026-08-05: make pr-open warned that #1628 textually conflicts with both #1626 (fix/lakesail-velox-compose-env-fallback) and #1618 (fix/uat-compose-project-name-budget) in exactly this file, and recovering #1628 hit the same conflict twice -- once cherry-picking onto develop and again rebasing after #1616 merged. Each occurrence is individually cheap (checkout --theirs, rerun the generator) but it is unavoidable, scales with concurrent UAT work, and the naive resolution -- hand-picking a side -- silently commits wrong numbers that only --check catches later.

preserves.behavior: CI still fails when the committed table drifts from the tree (uat_loc_table.py --check stays authoritative).
The spec keeps a human-readable per-module LOC breakdown in some form.

verifications.description: The generated table still matches the tree
verifications.expected: exit 0 on a clean tree; this guard must keep holding after any restructuring

verifications.description: Git knows how to merge the generated region without a hand resolution
